subject: RTBF / Deletion process & backups — next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RTBF / Deletion process & backups — recap and next steps

Hi Sophie — great to meet on the call this morning. Per our discovery, I wanted to recap the items we agreed on and next steps so your compliance and legal teams have a clear view.

Key takeaways: 
- Scope: FinTechCo wants the ability to submit Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) requests for end-user PII and for Redwood to fully purge associated inference logs.
- Timing expectation: Primary data deletion must be verifiable within 30 days of an RTBF request.
- Backups: You noted backups are governed by third-party cloud snapshots and you need clarity on our ability to delete from backups or provide attestations.
- Data residency: EU data must remain in EU regions for the requested tenant; most traffic today is US.

What we (Redwood) can commit to today (high level):
- Application-level purge: We can remove primary user records, cached KV entries, and any model-level tokenized traces within 30 days and provide a signed deletion certificate.
- Audit logs & metrics: We can redact PII from analytics traces and provide an event timeline; raw extensive logs are retained for debug windows (14–30 days) unless otherwise scoped.
- Backups & long-term snapshots: Default cloud snapshot retention is 90 days. We cannot instantaneously remove a named object from immutable multi-day snapshot chains without taking a longer retention pathway. However, we can offer a plan: scheduled expedited lifecycle for affected object IDs and a quarterly snapshot purge attestation.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marcus to run a 60-minute tech deep-dive with your infra team to map which objects (S3 keys, DB rows, inference traces) we need to purge and to surface any downstream copies.
2) Sophie/Rajesh to send a sanitized example of a RTBF request (fields you require in the certificate) and the internal SLA you expect.
3) We will share a deletion playbook draft and an estimate for shrinking backup retention for scoped tenants.

Attachments: FinTechCo_RTBF_Request.pdf (your template you shared), redwood-delete-playbook.pdf (initial draft).

I’ll leave Marcus and Laura on to cover technical and CSM next steps. Thanks —

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RTBF / Deletion process & backups — recap and next steps

Thanks Camila — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from Legal/Privacy: 

1) Certificate fields: We need the deletion certificate to include user ID (hashed), deletion timestamp, list of tables/keys deleted, and the operatorid that executed the job. Is Redwood able to include operatorid or an idempotent job id?

2) Backups: We understand cloud snapshot behavior. Two questions: a) can you provide a statement of your backup lifecycle scoped to our tenant, and b) can you offer a guaranteed timeline (e.g., 90 days) after which there are zero recoverable copies?

3) Audit & logs: If you redact PII from logs, can you confirm whether redaction is reversible by your team? (We prefer irreversible redaction or strong encryption where key is deleted.)

We’ll attach the RTBF template you requested — sending separately if the PDF is too big for email. Once Marcus proposes times, Rajesh and I can join the tech call.

— Sophie
Head of Privacy & Compliance | FinTechCo
(sophie.turner@fintechco.com)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@fintechco.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RTBF / Deletion process & backups — recap and next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks for the questions. Quick technical answers ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Deletion certificate: We can attach a job id and operator id for each purge run (operator id = service principal that initiated the job). Job ids are immutable and timestamped; we can include a hash of the user id rather than raw PII.

2) Backups & timeline: Our standard snapshot lifecycle in the public-hosted product is 90 days for full snapshots and 7–14 days for rolling incremental snapshots. We cannot surgically remove a single object from an already-written immutable snapshot chain. Options we can offer: 
   - Option A (attestation): Continue with 90-day retention and provide quarterly attestations that the tenant’s snapshots have rotated beyond the retention window (i.e., after 90 days, there are no recoverable snapshots containing the object).
   - Option B (shortened retention): For Dedicated or Private deployments we can negotiate a shorter snapshot retention (e.g., 30 days) implemented via lifecycle policy — this usually requires enterprise contract changes.
   - Option C (compensating control): On RTBF, we can zero-out or cryptographically erase the pointers inside our store and delete keys; while the physical blocks may remain in older backups, the data will be unrecoverable without the key (we can provide KMS key destruction attestation if customer-managed keys are used).

3) Logs & redaction: We support irreversible redaction for PII fields in operational logs (we overwrite fields and delete originals from fast stores). For analytics buckets, we can also apply one-way hashing. If you require key destruction guarantees, we recommend customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) so you control revocation.

Proposed time for technical deep-dive: Thu 12 Mar 2026 10:00–11:00 PT. Please let me know if that works. I’ll prep a short agenda and a mapping template for S3 keys / DB tables / inference traces.

— Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
